title: Method for assessing the content of molybdenum enzymes in fish internal organs
author: Satkanov, Tazhibay, et al.

steps.title: Harvest and freeze fish organs
steps.instruction: Rear African sharptooth catfish for two months under aquaponic conditions (water pH 7.5 ± 0.5, TAN 0.048 mg L⁻¹, nitrite 0.92 mg L⁻¹, nitrate 20 mg L⁻¹). Euthanize fish by exsanguination, dissect, collect the desired organs, freeze them immediately in liquid nitrogen and store at –80 °C until use.

steps.title: Prepare N. crassa nit‑1 extract
steps.instruction: Filter cultivated N. crassa nit‑1 vegetative hyphae through a ceramic filter using a vacuum pump. Grind the filtered hyphae in a ceramic mortar with liquid nitrogen. Add homogenization buffer A (0.05 M K/Na‑phosphate, pH 7.0, 5 mM EDTA, 1 % NaCl, 1 mM PMSF) to obtain a homogeneous suspension. Sonicate the suspension for 60 s at maximum power on a Hielscher UP200S ultrasonic device while keeping the sample on crushed ice. Centrifuge at 20 000 rpm for 20 min at 4 °C and keep the supernatant as the N. crassa nit‑1 extract.

steps.title: Make cell‑free extract from fish organs
steps.instruction: Prepare Buffer B (5 mM reduced glutathione, 25 mM Na₂MoO₄, pH 7.6, 0.05 M K/Na‑phosphate, 5 mM EDTA, 1 % NaCl). Weigh each frozen organ sample, grind it in a ceramic mortar with liquid nitrogen, and add Buffer B at a ratio of 1 : 3 w/v. Sonicate the homogenate for 60 s at maximum power on the UP200S device with ice cooling. Centrifuge the suspension at 20 000 rpm for 10 min at +4 °C and collect the supernatant (first cell‑free extract).

steps.title: Heat‑treat MoCo source
steps.instruction: Transfer the supernatant obtained above (MoCo source) to a water bath set at 80 °C and incubate for 3 min. Immediately cool on ice. Centrifuge the heated sample at 5 000 rpm for 5 min at +4 °C and keep the supernatant, which contains the isolated MoCo.

steps.title: Incubate extract with NADPH and MoCo
steps.instruction: Thaw the N. crassa nit‑1 extract on ice or at +4 °C. Add NADPH to the extract and incubate at room temperature for 5 min. Then add the freshly prepared MoCo source and incubate further for 15 min at room temperature to allow complementation of the apo‑enzyme.

steps.title: Add substrate, FAD and react
steps.instruction: Add nitrate (NO₃⁻), K/Na‑phosphate buffer (to maintain constant pH), and FAD to the mixture. Incubate the reaction at room temperature for 20 min, during which NO₃⁻ is reduced to NO₂⁻ by the re‑activated nitrate reductase.

steps.title: Terminate reaction by boiling
steps.instruction: Place the reaction tube in a water bath at 100 °C for 6 min to stop the enzymatic reaction and degrade NADPH (which interferes with the Griess assay). After boiling, centrifuge briefly to pellet the denatured proteins and keep the clear supernatant.

steps.title: Perform Griess assay
steps.instruction: Add sulphanilamide (SA) and N‑(1‑naphthyl)ethylenediamine dihydrochloride (NEDD) to the cleared supernatant, mix and incubate at room temperature for 10 min. Measure the resulting color intensity at 548 nm with a spectrophotometer.

steps.title: Calculate Mo‑enzyme activity
steps.instruction: Subtract the blank absorbance (average of control wells) from each sample absorbance (X = ODsample – ODcontrol). Convert X to nitrite concentration (nM) using the calibration curve. Divide the nitrite concentration by the reaction time (t, the interval from FAD addition to the 100 °C incubation) to obtain activity in Units (nM · min⁻¹). Perform statistical analysis in GraphPad 8 using ANOVA with Tukey’s post‑test; verify normality with the Kolmogorov‑Smirnov test and consider p < 0.05 as significant.
